subject: Mutual Action Plan: onboarding checklist & deployment lane decision
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-08-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mutual Action Plan: onboarding checklist & deployment lane decision

Hi Mike / Aisha —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is a tightened Mutual Action Plan (CuraHealth_MAP_v2.xlsx) that aligns commercial milestones with the technical evaluation steps we discussed. High-level asks so we can finalize the hosting lane (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and a go/no-go timeline:

- Confirm data residency requirement (US-only, or EU for PHI) by EOD Friday (owner: CuraHealth)
- Target POC capacity: 1k concurrent inference RPS burst, 100 qps steady — confirm numbers or adjust (owner: Mike)
- Security gating: complete the short SOC2 evidence request we attached (owner: CuraHealth security)
- Perf eval: Redwood will run a 2-week hosted pilot (us-east-1) with your red-team prompts, then we compare latency/cost to a Dedicated configuration (owner: Redwood infra)
- Procurement: if Dedicated/Private is chosen, procurement docs needed by 2025-08-26 to meet a 09/15 go-live (owner: CuraHealth procurement)

Proposed evaluation timeline (in MAP sheet):
- 8/18: Pilot kick-off on hosted (baseline metrics)
- 8/25: Mid-pilot checkpoint (latency/cost/regressions)
- 9/02: Decision gateway — choose Hosted (fast path) or Dedicated/Private (procurement + setup)

If you want, we can run an ingress simulation to model egress costs for HIPAA workloads; that will help compare hosted vs private economics.

Attachments: CuraHealth_MAP_v2.xlsx, SOC2_evidence_request.pdf

Next step: Can you confirm residency and capacity by Friday so we lock the MAP dates?

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Solutions Director
Redwood Inference

From: Mike Stevens <mike.stevens@curahealth.com>

Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: onboarding checklist & deployment lane decision

Evelyn —

Appreciate the clear plan and the doc. Quick answers from our side: 
- Residency: We need EU residency for any PHI processing; non-PHI can live in US-east for the pilot.
- Capacity: The 1k burst / 100 steady looks right for phase 1. We may need ~300 steady by Q4.
- SOC2: we'll start filling the evidence request; security will need a week to compile artifacts.

One question: for the 2-week hosted pilot, will Redwood provide an isolated tenant so our test data isn't visible to other customers? We are comfortable with hosted for evaluation if data is logically separated and encrypted at rest with our KMS.

Also, can you share a rough delta for monthly cost between hosted and a small dedicated pool (2x A100 or equivalent)? We want to present ballpark numbers to procurement before the 8/26 cutoff.

Thanks —
Mike
Head of Platform
CuraHealth
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Stevens <mike.stevens@curahealth.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-08-17T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: onboarding checklist & deployment lane decision

Mike —

Short answers and a suggested technical path we can put in the MAP: 

1) Tenant isolation for hosted pilot: yes — we can provision a dedicated tenant with tenant-scoped keys and network egress rules. For PHI we recommend limiting the pilot to synthetic or redacted datasets unless you sign our enterprise data addendum and enable customer-managed KMS.

2) Cost delta (very rough, ballpark monthly):
   - Hosted (pilot, pay-as-you-go): $15k–$30k/month depending on token volume and peak concurrency (includes baseline infra + caching optimizations).
   - Dedicated (reserved 2x A100-ish): $45k–$60k/month (committed monthly, predictable throughput).
   - Private/on-prem (one-time infra + ops): Capex heavy — order of magnitude higher up-front, ongoing ops cost varies.

3) Recommended MAP lanes to keep open: 
   - Fast path: Hosted pilot (us-east) -> decision gateway -> Hosted GA (if residency non-PHI)
   - Mid path: Hosted pilot (us-east) -> Dedicated reserved capacity (if performance/cost wins)
   - Regulated path: Private deployment (EU) for PHI + long procurement runway (target Q4)

I've attached a compact hosting_comparison_chart.png and noted owners in the MAP sheet. Proposed owners and dates we can lock if CuraHealth confirms residency by 8/18.

If that sounds good, Evelyn — can you send the DocuSign for the enterprise addendum (customer-managed KMS) so security can review? That will unblock PHI pilot later.

--
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
